name: FIFA
description: The global governing body for football, organizing the men's and women's World Cups for national teams as well as the FIFA Club World Cup for the champions of each confederation.

name: CAF
description: Africa's confederation, organizing the Africa Cup of Nations for national teams and continental club competitions.

name: AFC
description: Asia's confederation, organizing the AFC Asian Cup for national teams and continental club competitions.

name: UEFA
description: Europe's governing body, running both the men's and women's national team championships and the continent's top club competitions.

name: CONCACAF
fullName: Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football
description: The confederation for North America, Central America and the Caribbean, organizing the CONCACAF Gold Cup for national teams and continental club competitions.

name: OFC
description: Oceania's confederation, the smallest of the six by membership and World Cup representation, organizing the OFC Nations Cup for national teams.

name: CONMEBOL
description: South America's confederation, organizing the Copa América for national teams and the Copa Libertadores for clubs.

name: AFF
description: The governing body for football in Afghanistan, a country where cricket has historically drawn more attention than football domestically.

name: AFA
description: The governing body for football in Albania, which reached its first-ever major tournament, Euro 2016.

name: AFF
description: The governing body for football in Algeria. Algeria's 1982 World Cup upset of West Germany was followed by West Germany and Austria playing out a mutually convenient 1-0 result that eliminated Algeria anyway — the collusion was so blatant it's remembered as the 'Disgrace of Gijón' and led FIFA to schedule final group games simultaneously ever since.

name: FFAS
description: The governing body for football in American Samoa, founded in 1984 and reorganized as FFAS in 2007. The national team holds football's all-time world record for the largest margin of defeat: 31-0 to Australia in a 2002 World Cup qualifier.

name: AFF
description: The governing body for football in Andorra, a microstate whose national team has one of the lowest win totals of any FIFA member.

name: AFF
description: The governing body for football in Angola, which hosted the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations.

name: AFA
description: The governing body for football in Anguilla, a British Overseas Territory.

name: ABFA
description: The governing body for football in Antigua and Barbuda.

name: AFA
description: The governing body for football in Argentina, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: FFA
description: The governing body for football in Armenia, established after independence from the Soviet Union.

name: AFF
description: The governing body for football in Aruba, a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

name: FA
description: The governing body for football in Australia, which moved from the OFC to the AFC in 2006 after decades as Oceania's dominant team, seeking tougher regular qualification for the World Cup.

name: AFA
description: The governing body for football in Austria, home to the 'Wunderteam' of the early 1930s, one of the most admired sides of the pre-war era.

name: AFFA
fullName: Association of Football Federations of Azerbaijan
description: The governing body for football in Azerbaijan, established after independence from the Soviet Union.

name: BFA
description: The governing body for football in the Bahamas.

name: BFA
description: The governing body for football in Bahrain.

name: BFF
description: The governing body for football in Bangladesh, established the same year the country gained independence.

name: BFA
description: The governing body for football in Barbados. The national team is the answer to a famous piece of footballing trivia: in a 1994 Caribbean Cup qualifier against Grenada, Barbados deliberately scored an own goal to exploit a tournament rule awarding extra value to golden-goal wins, then defended both ends of the pitch to force (and win) the golden-goal period.

name: FFB
description: The governing body for football in Belarus, established shortly before the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

name: RBFA
description: The governing body for football in Belgium. A golden generation led by Kevin De Bruyne and Eden Hazard took the 'Red Devils' to the top of the FIFA World Rankings and a World Cup semifinal in 2018.

name: FFB
description: The governing body for football in Belize, the smallest football nation on the Central American mainland by population.

name: BFF
description: The governing body for football in Benin.

name: BFA
description: The governing body for football in Bermuda.

name: BFF
description: The governing body for football in Bhutan. In 2002, the Bhutanese national team played Montserrat in 'The Other Final' — a specially arranged match between the two lowest-ranked teams in the world, staged on the same day as that year's FIFA World Cup Final.

name: BFF
description: The governing body for football in Bolivia, whose only Copa América title came in 1963, hosted at altitude in La Paz. The national stadium's elevation (over 3,500 metres, and as high as 4,000+ metres at an alternate venue used for qualifiers) has long been a genuine home advantage — so much so that FIFA briefly banned World Cup qualifiers above 2,500 metres in 2007 before reversing the decision.

name: BFF
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. Full CONCACAF member since 2014 (associate since 2013).
description: The governing body for football in Bonaire, a special municipality of the Netherlands in the Caribbean.

name: FFBH
fullName: Football Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The governing body for football in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which reached its first-ever World Cup in 2014 as an independent nation.

name: BFA
description: The governing body for football in Botswana.

name: CBF
description: The governing body for football in Brazil, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: BVIFA
description: The governing body for football in the British Virgin Islands.

name: FABD
description: The governing body for football in Brunei. The original Brunei Football Association, founded in 1952, was dissolved in 2008 amid administrative disputes; the current Football Association of Brunei Darussalam was established in 2011.

name: BFU
description: The governing body for football in Bulgaria, which reached the 1994 World Cup semifinals behind Hristo Stoichkov's Golden Boot-winning tournament.

name: BFF
description: The governing body for football in Burkina Faso, whose national team reached the Africa Cup of Nations final in 2013.

name: FFB
description: The governing body for football in Burundi.

name: FFC
description: The governing body for football in Cambodia.

name: CFF
description: The governing body for football in Cameroon. The 'Indomitable Lions' became the first African team to reach a World Cup quarterfinal in 1990, with Roger Milla's corner-flag goal celebrations turning him into one of the tournament's most memorable figures at age 38.

name: Canada Soccer
description: The governing body for football in Canada, overseeing the national teams and the domestic league and cup system.

name: CVFF
description: The governing body for football in Cape Verde. One of the smallest nations by population ever to reach the Africa Cup of Nations, Cape Verde made the quarterfinals in its tournament debut in 2013.

name: CIFA
description: The governing body for football in the Cayman Islands.

name: CAFF
description: The governing body for football in the Central African Republic.

name: CFF
description: The governing body for football in Chad.

name: CFF
description: The governing body for football in Chile. Hosting the 1962 World Cup, the national team reached its best-ever result, the semifinals, before winning back-to-back Copa América titles in 2015 and 2016 — the country's first-ever major trophies.

name: CFA
description: The governing body for football in China.

name: CTFA
description: The governing body for football in Chinese Taipei (Taiwan), which competes internationally under that name due to political sensitivities around the island's status.

name: FCF
description: The governing body for football in Colombia, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: CFF
description: The governing body for football in Comoros, one of the smallest nations ever to qualify for the Africa Cup of Nations — reached in 2021, its tournament debut.

name: CFF
description: The governing body for football in the Republic of the Congo, which won the Africa Cup of Nations in 1972 as Congo-Brazzaville.

name: CIFA
description: The governing body for football in the Cook Islands, spread across 2 million square kilometers of ocean — its furthest-flung member association, Pukapuka, is closer to Samoa than to the federation's own headquarters in Rarotonga.

name: FCRF
description: The governing body for football in Costa Rica, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: CFF
description: The governing body for football in Croatia. In just their second-ever World Cup as an independent nation, Croatia reached the 2018 final, and added a third-place finish in 2022.

name: FAC
description: The governing body for football in Cuba. Political isolation has long limited the national team's international schedule, and several Cuban squads have lost players to defection while on tour abroad.

name: CFF
description: The governing body for football in Curaçao, formed after the 2010 dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles. The national team, nicknamed the Blue Wave, reached the 2023 Gold Cup quarterfinals in just its second decade of independent existence.

name: CFA
description: The governing body for football in Cyprus.

name: FACR
fullName: Football Association of the Czech Republic
description: The governing body for football in Czechia, continuing the football lineage of the former Czechoslovakia, twice a World Cup runner-up (1934, 1962).

name: CAFF
description: The governing body for football in DR Congo, the oldest federation in CAF. As Zaire, the team won the Africa Cup of Nations twice (1968, 1974) and became the first Sub-Saharan African nation to reach a World Cup, in 1974.

name: DFA
description: The governing body for football in Denmark. Denmark weren't even supposed to be at Euro 1992 — they were called up as a late replacement after Yugoslavia was banned due to war, with several players recalled from vacation — and went on to win the entire tournament.

name: DFF
description: The governing body for football in Djibouti.

name: DFA
description: The governing body for football in Dominica.

name: DFF
description: The governing body for football in the Dominican Republic, a country where baseball has traditionally overshadowed football but where the sport's popularity has grown significantly in recent decades.

name: EFF
description: The governing body for football in Ecuador, whose national team has reached the World Cup knockout stage on multiple occasions since its qualifying breakthrough in 2002.

name: EFA
description: The governing body for football in Egypt, a founding member of CAF, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: SFA
description: The governing body for football in El Salvador. A 1969 World Cup qualifier against Honduras coincided with rising tensions between the two countries, giving the brief war that followed weeks later its enduring nickname: the Football War.

name: FA
description: The governing body for football in England, the oldest national football association in the world, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup pyramid.

name: EFF
description: The governing body for football in Equatorial Guinea, which co-hosted the 2012 Africa Cup of Nations with Gabon.

name: ENFF
description: The governing body for football in Eritrea. Several Eritrean national squads have seen multiple players seek asylum abroad while on international duty, at times leaving the team unable to field a full squad for later matches.

name: EFA
description: The governing body for football in Estonia.

name: EFA
description: The governing body for football in Eswatini.

name: EFF
description: The governing body for football in Ethiopia. Ethiopia's only Africa Cup of Nations title came in 1962, hosting the tournament and beating Egypt 4-2 after extra time in the final.

name: FIFA
description: The governing body for football in the Faroe Islands. In their first-ever competitive match in 1990 — fielding a team of amateurs — the Faroe Islands beat an Austria side that had played at the World Cup just three months earlier, one of the biggest shocks in football history.

name: FFA
description: The governing body for football in Fiji, overseeing the national team and the domestic league system.

name: FAF
description: The governing body for football in Finland, which reached its first-ever major tournament, Euro 2020, after decades as one of Europe's perennial qualifying near-misses.

name: FFF
description: The governing body for football in France, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: LFG
fullName: Ligue de Football de la Guyane
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. Full CONCACAF member since 2013 (associate since 1978).
description: The governing body for football in French Guiana, an overseas region of France in South America affiliated with CONCACAF rather than CONMEBOL for geopolitical reasons.

name: GFF
description: The governing body for football in Gabon, which co-hosted the 2012 Africa Cup of Nations with Equatorial Guinea and hosted again alone in 2017.

name: GFA
description: The governing body for football in the Gambia, one of Africa's smallest nations by population, which reached the Africa Cup of Nations for the first time in 2022.

name: GFF
description: The governing body for football in Georgia, which reached its first-ever major tournament, Euro 2024, as co-hosts of the delayed qualifying playoff format.

name: DFB
description: The governing body for football in Germany, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: GFA
description: The governing body for football in Ghana. The 'Black Stars' came within a missed penalty of the 2010 World Cup semifinal — the last-gasp handball that denied them a certain winning goal against Uruguay, and the penalty Asamoah Gyan struck against the crossbar in the shootout that followed, remain one of the tournament's most painful what-ifs.

name: GFA
description: The governing body for football in Gibraltar, a British Overseas Territory that became UEFA's newest member in 2013 after a long legal battle over its eligibility.

name: HFF
description: The governing body for football in Greece, whose national team pulled off one of football's biggest-ever shocks by winning Euro 2004 as 150-1 outsiders.

name: GFA
description: The governing body for football in Grenada.

name: LGF
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. Full CONCACAF member since 2013 (associate since 1964).
description: The governing body for football in Guadeloupe, a French overseas department in the Caribbean.

name: GFA
description: The governing body for football in Guam, a US territory.

name: NFFG
description: The governing body for football in Guatemala, one of the oldest federations in Central America.

name: GFF
description: The governing body for football in Guinea.

name: FFGB
description: The governing body for football in Guinea-Bissau.

name: GFF
description: The governing body for football in Guyana — one of the oldest federations in the Americas despite the national team never having qualified for a World Cup. Guyana plays in CONCACAF rather than CONMEBOL, one of three South American nations (with Suriname and French Guiana) grouped there for geopolitical reasons.

name: HFF
description: The governing body for football in Haiti, a founding member of CONCACAF in 1961. Haiti was the first Caribbean nation to qualify for a men's FIFA World Cup, in 1974.

name: NAFFH
fullName: National Autonomous Federation of Football of Honduras
description: The governing body for football in Honduras, rebranded from FENAFUTH to FFH in 2024. The other side of El Salvador's 1969 'Football War,' a qualifying-match rivalry that coincided with a genuine armed conflict between the two countries.

name: HKFA
description: The governing body for football in Hong Kong, one of Asia's oldest football federations and host of the AFC's founding congress in 1954.

name: HFF
description: The governing body for football in Hungary. The 'Mighty Magyars' of the 1950s, led by Ferenc Puskás, went unbeaten for over four years and are widely considered one of the greatest teams never to win a World Cup, losing the 1954 final to West Germany.

name: FAI
description: The governing body for football in Iceland. At Euro 2016, the smallest nation ever to reach a major tournament's quarterfinals beat England along the way — a result so shocking it prompted England's manager to resign within hours.

name: AIFF
description: The governing body for football in India, a cricket-dominant nation where football nonetheless has a passionate following, particularly in West Bengal, Kerala and the northeast.

name: FAI
description: The governing body for football in Indonesia, whose passionate, enormous fanbase has made its domestic league one of the most attended in Asia despite the national team's modest international results.

name: FFIRI
fullName: Football Federation Islamic Republic of Iran
description: The governing body for football in Iran, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: IFA
description: The governing body for football in Iraq. The national team won the 2007 AFC Asian Cup — its only major title — beating Saudi Arabia in the final amid the ongoing Iraq War, a result celebrated as a rare moment of national unity.

name: IFA
confederationHistory: Ex-AFC member (1954–1974), became a full UEFA member in 1994.
description: The governing body for football in Israel, expelled from the AFC in 1974 amid a boycott by Arab and Muslim member associations and eventually admitted as a full UEFA member in 1994.

name: IFF
description: The governing body for football in Italy. The 'Azzurri' have won four World Cups, second only to Brazil, but stunningly failed to qualify for the tournament altogether in both 2018 and 2022.

name: IFF
description: The governing body for football in Ivory Coast. The 'Elephants,' led for years by Didier Drogba, won the Africa Cup of Nations in 2015 and again as hosts in 2024.

name: JFF
description: The governing body for football in Jamaica. The 'Reggae Boyz' became the first English-speaking Caribbean nation to reach a men's FIFA World Cup, in 1998.

name: JFA
description: The governing body for football in Japan, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: JFA
description: The governing body for football in Jordan, whose national team reached its first-ever AFC Asian Cup final in 2024, losing to hosts Qatar.

name: FFK
description: The governing body for football in Kazakhstan, which spent its first decade of independence as an AFC member before switching to UEFA in 2002, seeking more regular, higher-quality competition.

name: FKF
description: The governing body for football in Kenya.

name: KIFA
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. OFC associate member since 2007.
description: The governing body for football in Kiribati.

name: FFK
description: The governing body for football in Kosovo, admitted to FIFA and UEFA in 2016 after a long campaign for international recognition following independence in 2008.

name: KFA
description: The governing body for football in Kuwait, winner of the 1980 AFC Asian Cup.

name: FFKR
fullName: Football Federation of the Kyrgyz Republic
description: The governing body for football in Kyrgyzstan, established after independence from the Soviet Union.

name: LFF
description: The governing body for football in Laos.

name: LFF
description: The governing body for football in Latvia.

name: LFA
description: The governing body for football in Lebanon, whose national team draws players from a large Lebanese diaspora across the world.

name: LFA
description: The governing body for football in Lesotho.

name: LFA
description: The governing body for football in Liberia. George Weah, the only African-born winner of the Ballon d'Or (1995), later became Liberia's president in 2018.

name: LFF
description: The governing body for football in Libya.

name: LFA
description: The governing body for football in Liechtenstein, a microstate with no top-flight domestic league of its own — its clubs play in the Swiss league system instead, while the national team competes independently in FIFA and UEFA competitions.

name: LFF
description: The governing body for football in Lithuania.

name: LFF
description: The governing body for football in Luxembourg.

name: MFA
description: The governing body for football in Macau, a special administrative region of China.

name: MFF
description: The governing body for football in Madagascar, whose national team reached the Africa Cup of Nations quarterfinals in its tournament debut in 2019.

name: FAM
description: The governing body for football in Malawi.

name: FAM
description: The governing body for football in Malaysia.

name: FAM
description: The governing body for football in the Maldives.

name: MFF
description: The governing body for football in Mali.

name: MFA
description: The governing body for football in Malta.

name: LFM
fullName: Ligue de football de la Martinique
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. Full CONCACAF member since 2013 (associate since 1978).
description: The governing body for football in Martinique, a French overseas department in the Caribbean.

name: FFIRM
fullName: Football Federation of the Islamic Republic of Mauritania
description: The governing body for football in Mauritania.

name: MFA
description: The governing body for football in Mauritius.

name: FMF
description: The governing body for football in Mexico, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: FAM
description: The governing body for football in Moldova, established shortly before independence from the Soviet Union.

name: MFF
description: The governing body for football in Mongolia, a country where wrestling and archery have traditionally overshadowed football.

name: FAM
description: The governing body for football in Montenegro, established after independence from Serbia and Montenegro in 2006.

name: MFA
description: The governing body for football in Montserrat. In 2002, the national team played Bhutan in 'The Other Final' — a specially arranged match between the two lowest-ranked teams in the world, staged on the same day as that year's FIFA World Cup Final.

name: FRMF
description: The governing body for football in Morocco, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: MFF
description: The governing body for football in Mozambique.

name: MFF
description: The governing body for football in Myanmar, established the same year the country gained independence from Britain.

name: NFA
description: The governing body for football in Namibia.

name: ANFA
description: The governing body for football in Nepal.

name: RDFA
description: The governing body for football in the Netherlands. The 'Total Football' teams of the 1970s, and later sides featuring Van Basten, Bergkamp and Robben, made the Dutch the most celebrated team never to win a World Cup — losing three finals (1974, 1978, 2010) without ever lifting the trophy.

name: NCFF
description: The governing body for football in New Caledonia, founded in 1928 but not affiliated to FIFA until 2004 — a 76-year gap. The national team reached the final of the 2012 OFC Nations Cup, losing to Tahiti.

name: NZF
description: The governing body for football in New Zealand, historically the dominant national team in Oceania.

name: NFF
description: The governing body for football in Nicaragua, a country where football has historically taken a back seat to baseball as the national sport.

name: NFF
description: The governing body for football in Niger.

name: NFF
description: The governing body for football in Nigeria, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: DKFA
description: The governing body for football in North Korea. The 1966 World Cup team became the first Asian side ever to reach the quarterfinals, famously beating Italy 1-0 in the group stage along the way.

name: FFM
description: The governing body for football in North Macedonia, which reached its first-ever major tournament, Euro 2020, as one of the competition's smallest-ever qualifiers.

name: IFA
description: The governing body for football in Northern Ireland. Managed by Billy Bingham and inspired by a teenage Norman Whiteside, Northern Ireland reached the 1982 World Cup quarterfinals, famously beating hosts Spain along the way.

name: NMIFA
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member, despite being a full AFC member since 2020 (the AFC's 47th) — FIFA membership requires a separate application, submitted in 2021 but not yet granted.
description: The governing body for football in the Northern Mariana Islands, a US territory.

name: FAN
description: The governing body for football in Norway.

name: OFA
description: The governing body for football in Oman.

name: PFF
description: The governing body for football in Pakistan, established the same year the country gained independence, in a nation where cricket dominates public attention.

name: PFA
description: The governing body for football in Palestine, one of FIFA's oldest member associations — affiliated since 1929 — despite the absence of a fully sovereign Palestinian state.

name: PFF
description: The governing body for football in Panama. The national team's first-ever World Cup qualification, in 2018, was completed in dramatic fashion with a stoppage-time goal against Costa Rica.

name: PNGFA
description: The governing body for football in Papua New Guinea, overseeing the national team and the domestic league system.

name: PFA
description: The governing body for football in Paraguay. The national team reached its best-ever World Cup result, the 2010 quarterfinals, before narrowly losing 1-0 to eventual champions Spain.

name: PFF
description: The governing body for football in Peru. Led by Teófilo Cubillas, Peru reached the 1970 World Cup quarterfinals — but after 1982, the team went 36 years without qualifying again, finally returning at the 2018 tournament.

name: PFF
description: The governing body for football in the Philippines, one of Asia's oldest federations, in a country where basketball is the dominant sport.

name: PFA
description: The governing body for football in Poland, which reached back-to-back World Cup semifinals in 1974 and 1982 behind striker Grzegorz Lato.

name: PFF
description: The governing body for football in Portugal. Eusébio inspired the country to a World Cup semifinal on debut in 1966; six decades later, Cristiano Ronaldo led Portugal to its first major title at Euro 2016.

name: PRFF
description: The governing body for football in Puerto Rico, a US territory that competes as its own separate CONCACAF member rather than as part of the United States.

name: QFA
description: The governing body for football in Qatar, which hosted and won the 2023 AFC Asian Cup and hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup — the first World Cup held in the Middle East.

name: FAI
description: The governing body for football in the Republic of Ireland. Under Jack Charlton, Ireland reached the World Cup quarterfinals in 1990, its first-ever appearance at the tournament.

name: RFF
description: The governing body for football in Romania, whose 'Golden Generation' led by Gheorghe Hagi reached the 1994 World Cup quarterfinals.

name: RFU
description: The governing body for football in Russia, suspended from FIFA and UEFA competitions since 2022 following the invasion of Ukraine.

name: RAFF
description: The governing body for football in Rwanda.

name: LRF
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. CAF associate member since 1992.
description: The governing body for football in Réunion, a French overseas department in the Indian Ocean.

name: SKNFA
fullName: St. Kitts and Nevis Football Association
description: The governing body for football in Saint Kitts and Nevis.

name: SLFA
description: The governing body for football in Saint Lucia.

name: LFSM
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. Full CONCACAF member since 2013 (associate since 2002), representing the French half of the island of Saint Martin.
description: The governing body for football in the French Collectivity of Saint Martin, sharing the Caribbean island of Saint Martin with Sint Maarten.

name: SVGFF
fullName: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Football Federation
description: The governing body for football in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

name: FFS
description: The governing body for football in Samoa, affiliated to FIFA and the OFC since 1986.

name: SMFF
description: The governing body for football in San Marino, one of the smallest football nations in the world, whose national team has one of the poorest overall records of any FIFA member.

name: SAFF
description: The governing body for football in Saudi Arabia, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: SFA
description: The governing body for football in Scotland, the second-oldest national football association in the world. Scotland and England contested the first-ever international football match in 1872.

name: SFF
description: The governing body for football in Senegal. The 'Lions of Teranga' stunned defending champions France in their opening match of the 2002 World Cup, and won their first Africa Cup of Nations title in 2021 behind captain Sadio Mané.

name: FAS
description: The governing body for football in Serbia, continuing the football lineage of Yugoslavia, a European Championship runner-up in 1960 and 1968.

name: SFF
description: The governing body for football in Seychelles.

name: SLFA
description: The governing body for football in Sierra Leone.

name: FAS
description: The governing body for football in Singapore, one of the oldest football associations in Asia.

name: SXMFF
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member — a 2016 membership application was rejected, and the federation has since taken the dispute to the Court of Arbitration for Sport. Full CONCACAF member since 2013 (associate since 2002).
description: The governing body for football in Sint Maarten, a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands sharing the Caribbean island of Saint Martin with the French Collectivity of Saint Martin.

name: SFA
description: The governing body for football in Slovakia, continuing the football lineage of the former Czechoslovakia after splitting from the Czech Republic in 1993.

name: FAS
description: The governing body for football in Slovenia, which reached the World Cup in just its second attempt as an independent nation, in 2002.

name: SIFF
description: The governing body for football in the Solomon Islands. The national team's best-ever World Cup qualifying run came in 2004-05, reaching the final Oceania playoff round against Australia before being eliminated 11-1 on aggregate.

name: SFF
description: The governing body for football in Somalia, where the national team has continued competing internationally despite decades of civil conflict at home.

name: SAFA
description: The governing body for football in South Africa, a founding member of CAF, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: KFA
description: The governing body for football in South Korea, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: SSFA
description: The governing body for football in South Sudan, established the same year the country gained independence — one of the newest national football federations in the world.

name: RFEF
description: The governing body for football in Spain, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: FFSL
description: The governing body for football in Sri Lanka, a cricket-dominant nation where football nonetheless has a long history dating to the colonial era.

name: SFA
description: The governing body for football in Sudan, which hosted and won the Africa Cup of Nations in 1970 — the country's only title.

name: SFA
description: The governing body for football in Suriname, one of three South American nations (with Guyana and French Guiana) that plays in CONCACAF rather than CONMEBOL. Dutch colonial ties mean a striking number of Suriname-eligible players, including several full internationals, have instead represented the Netherlands.

name: SFA
description: The governing body for football in Sweden, which hosted the 1958 World Cup and reached the final, losing to a Brazil side inspired by a 17-year-old Pelé.

name: SFA
description: The governing body for football in Switzerland, headquartered in Bern despite hosting FIFA and UEFA's own headquarters elsewhere in the country.

name: SFA
description: The governing body for football in Syria. Amid the country's civil war, the national team has played most of its 'home' World Cup qualifiers at neutral venues abroad for well over a decade.

name: STFF
description: The governing body for football in São Tomé and Príncipe.

name: TFF
description: The governing body for football in Tahiti (French Polynesia). Tahiti won the 2012 OFC Nations Cup and went on to represent Oceania at the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup in Brazil — the smallest footballing nation ever to play in a FIFA tournament alongside the world's top teams.

name: TFF
description: The governing body for football in Tajikistan.

name: TFF
description: The governing body for football in Tanzania.

name: FAT
description: The governing body for football in Thailand, historically the dominant football nation in Southeast Asia's ASEAN region.

name: ETFF
description: The governing body for football in Timor-Leste, established the same year the country gained independence — one of Asia's newest football federations.

name: TFF
description: The governing body for football in Togo. Ahead of the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations, the team bus was attacked by gunmen while crossing into the tournament's host region, killing three people connected to the squad; Togo withdrew from the competition in the aftermath.

name: TFA
description: The governing body for football in Tonga, affiliated to FIFA and the OFC since 1994.

name: TTFA
description: The governing body for football in Trinidad and Tobago. The 'Soca Warriors' remain the smallest nation by population ever to qualify for a men's FIFA World Cup, reaching the 2006 tournament in Germany.

name: TFF
description: The governing body for football in Tunisia. In 1978, Tunisia became the first African and Arab nation to win a World Cup match, beating Mexico 3-1 — they'd go on to win the 2004 Africa Cup of Nations on home soil.

name: FFT
description: The governing body for football in Turkmenistan, established after independence from the Soviet Union.

name: TCIFA
fullName: Turks and Caicos Islands Football Association
description: The governing body for football in the Turks and Caicos Islands.

name: TIFA
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. OFC associate member since 2019.
description: The governing body for football in Tuvalu.

name: TFF
description: The governing body for football in Türkiye. The national team finished third at the 2002 World Cup, its first appearance in the tournament since 1954.

name: UVISF
description: The governing body for football in the U.S. Virgin Islands.

name: FUFA
description: The governing body for football in Uganda, one of the oldest federations in CAF. The 'Cranes' were Africa Cup of Nations runners-up in 1978.

name: FFU
description: The governing body for football in Ukraine, established the same year the country gained independence from the Soviet Union. Ukraine has continued competing in FIFA and UEFA competitions throughout the ongoing war following Russia's 2022 invasion.

name: UAEFA
description: The governing body for football in the United Arab Emirates, established the same year the country was formed.

name: USSF
description: The governing body for football in the United States, overseeing the national teams and the domestic league and cup system.

name: AUF
description: The governing body for football in Uruguay, overseeing the national team and the domestic league and cup system.

name: UFF
description: The governing body for football in Uzbekistan.

name: VFF
description: The governing body for football in Vanuatu, overseeing the national team and the domestic league system.

name: VFF
description: The governing body for football in Venezuela, a country where baseball has traditionally overshadowed football. Venezuela remains the only CONMEBOL nation to have never qualified for a men's FIFA World Cup.

name: VFF
description: The governing body for football in Vietnam.

name: FAW
description: The governing body for football in Wales, the third-oldest national football association in the world. Led by Gareth Bale, Wales reached the Euro 2016 semifinals — its first major tournament in 58 years.

name: YFA
description: The governing body for football in Yemen, where the ongoing civil war has severely disrupted the national team's ability to play home matches or train together as a full squad.

name: FAZ
description: The governing body for football in Zambia. In 1993, a plane carrying most of the national team crashed off the coast of Gabon, killing all 30 aboard. Zambia won its only Africa Cup of Nations title in 2012 — hosted, fittingly, in Gabon, with the final played a few hundred metres from the crash site.

name: ZFF
fifaAffiliation: Not a FIFA member. CAF associate member since 2004 — briefly admitted as a full CAF member in 2017, but membership was rescinded after four months since CAF could not recognise two separate associations (Zanzibar and Tanzania) from one FIFA-member country.
description: The governing body for football in Zanzibar, a semi-autonomous part of Tanzania. Founded in 1926, 19 years before mainland Tanzania's own federation.

name: ZFA
description: The governing body for football in Zimbabwe.
